subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram inline buttons for pairing approve/deny

question: What authorization model should Telegram pairing approve/deny buttons use for operator-device and browser/Control UI requests that may require operator.admin?
rationale: A button is easy to render, but resolving it can grant device/browser access; automation should not decide whether command-owner Telegram identity is enough, whether an admin-scoped paired device is still required, or how this aligns with broader channel-aware approval work.

options.title: Typed pairing approval cards
options.body: Create a device-pair-owned card/action contract that Telegram renders as buttons and that resolves only after the existing pairing scope/admin checks pass.

options.title: Defer to channel-aware scope upgrade design
options.body: Keep this issue open but wait for the broader channel-aware approval-card direction before adding a Telegram-specific path.

options.title: Keep command-only approval
options.body: Decline inline approval for pairing and keep explicit `/pair approve` or CLI approval as the supported security posture.

recommendation.title: Typed pairing approval cards
recommendation.body: Create a device-pair-owned card/action contract that Telegram renders as buttons and that resolves only after the existing pairing scope/admin checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent main history on both the device-pair and Telegram callback surfaces makes this the best current routing candidate, with security review still needed.
